title: Spiced Masala Chai with Ginger and Cardamom
summary: Cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, peppercorns and star anise are cracked and toasted, simmered with ginger and strong black tea, then boiled with milk and a little sugar and strained.
equipment: heavy frying pan or rolling pin, for crushing

ingredients.item: fresh ginger, thinly sliced (no need to peel)
strong loose black tea, such as Assam

steps.title: Crack the spices
steps.text: Put the cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, peppercorns and star anise on a board and press down hard with the base of a heavy pan until coarsely cracked. Cracking opens the pods and releases their oils.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Tip the spices into the saucepan and toast over medium heat, stirring, for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.

steps.title: Simmer with tea
steps.text: Add the water and ginger, bring to the boil, then lower the heat and simmer for 5 minutes. Add the tea and simmer for 3 minutes more, until very dark.

steps.title: Boil with milk
steps.text: Pour in the milk and sugar, bring back to a lively boil and cook for 2 minutes, watching closely as milk tea boils over in seconds.

steps.title: Strain and serve
steps.text: Strain through the sieve into the jug, pressing on the tea leaves, and pour into 4 mugs.

tips: Use a strong, malty tea such as Assam; delicate teas get lost under the milk and spices.
Lift the pan off the heat for a moment if the chai rises; it settles straight away.
Adjust the sugar at the end; chai is traditionally quite sweet, but this version is lightly sweetened.
For a stronger spice hit, add an extra slice of ginger rather than more tea, which turns bitter.
storage: Best fresh. Refrigerate leftovers, covered, for up to 2 days and reheat until steaming. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
